newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO under pressure on dwindling demand.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO under pressure on dwindling demand.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices were assessed lower as demand continued to dwindle in the absence of support from crude levels, traders said on Tuesday.
NYMEX February crude prices saw a marginal rise of just 10 cents and last traded at $25.29 per barrel.
Traders said the marginal support would not be enough to pull prices out of the doldrums.
"Demand remained weak," said a trader. "We see very little buying interest from China."
On supplies, Kuwait would export its usual volume of three cargoes after exporting four in February, traders said.
Some traders said they remained uncertain of price trends and are waiting if prices would bottom out before moving any cargoes.
Support from bunkers was also lacking, a trader said.
Eyes were also on Taiwan's import tender for February-delivery fuel oil which closes on Wednesday.
Traders said the awarded price would provide a clearer indicator of where the market is. Some traders hope that the import tender would also stem the price slide.
Physical prices for end-January lifting supplies were quoted at $117-$119 per tonne on Tuesday.
In the swaps market, front-month January was last quoted at $115/$116 per tonne, down from Monday's $115.75/$116.75.
